title: Self-serve Network Readiness Auto-Triage and Prescriptive Remediation Playbook for Private Deploys
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Enterprise customers requesting Private/VPC/on-prem deployments frequently hit inconsistent triage outcomes for networking and air-gapped constraints. Manual intake is slow, opaque to customers, and causes repeated engineering rework. This ticket scopes a self-serve network readiness auto-triage feature coupled with a prescriptive remediation playbook surfaced in the Console and the onboarding portal. Goal: reduce manual intake time by 60%, surface deterministic pass/fail reasons, and provide runnable remediation steps customers can use or hand to their infra teams.
acceptance_criteria: Console: new 'Network Readiness' card visible on Private Onboarding flow that runs a deterministic probe and returns a readiness score (0-100)
Auto-triage: system classifies failure modes into <networking>, <upgrade-constraints>, <airgap-missing-reqs> with human-readable explanations and recommended fixes
Remediation: for top 8 failure modes provide 1-click download of remediation script or a copy/paste checklist plus a suggested engagement template for SEs
Telemetry: each triage run emits structured events for metrics (time-to-resolve, common failure modes) and links to customer ticket/ID
Security: probe runs are read-only and use customer-provided ephemeral credentials; security review and KMS gating documented
Workflow: Console allows customer to mark 'remediation applied' and re-run probe; re-run history retained for 90 days
proposed_solution: Build a lightweight probe agent (containerized) customers can run in their VPC or air-gapped environment. The agent performs deterministic checks (DNS egress, outbound IPs, TLS handshake to collector, registry access, kernel module checks for HSM/KMS, proxy path validation) and uploads a signed report to the control plane when permitted. The control plane will run a rule engine that maps probe outputs to curated failure categories and suggested remediation steps. Surface results in Console with links to remediation artifacts and an option to share results with Redwood SE securely.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Agent vs remote probes: agent is higher trust but required for strict air-gapped; remote probes are lower friction but miss internal network rules
Deep vs shallow checks: deep checks give clearer guidance but increase agent surface area and security review scope; initial release will prioritize shallow deterministic checks
Self-serve vs full-SE assisted: self-serve accelerates onboarding for smaller customers but complex enterprise setups will still route to SE-led lane
implementation_phases: Phase 1 (MVP): Console UI, shallow agent with DNS/egress/registry checks, rule engine for top 5 failure categories, downloadable remediation scripts
Phase 2: Expand checks (KMS/HSM, proxy auth flows), add historical runs and report sharing, automate remediation where safe
Phase 3: Add canary gating integration for staged upgrades and automated SLA gating for Dedicated customers
open_questions: What minimal set of checks satisfy legal/regulatory auditors for air-gapped onboarding?
Are customers allowed to upload full packet captures if they opt-in?
How should sensitive telemetry be redacted before being stored in our control plane?
